title: Fractured phase scheduler: kernel-probe feedback and fractional prefill splits for tenant fairness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Latency-sensitive tenants (interactive chat/agents) are being penalized by coarse-grained prefill/decode scheduling that favors large throughput-oriented batches. Meanwhile, kernel-selection heuristics do not get real-time feedback from request phases to pick specialized attention kernels or micro-quantized paths. This ticket designs and validates a fractured-phase scheduler that: (1) probes kernel cost/latency early in the prefill phase, (2) allows fractional splitting of a single request into micro-phases with different routing policies, and (3) applies tenant-aware crediting so latency-critical tenants get bounded P95 while preserving throughput of batchy workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Offline simulation showing >=15% reduction in P95 latency for latency-critical tenants compared to baseline scheduler, while throughput (tokens/sec) for batch tenants drops by <=5%
End-to-end prototype integrated into runtime with kernel-probe telemetry emitting per-phase latency and kernel choice signals
A/B experiment plan defined and dashboard widgets created to track per-tenant P50/P95, tokens/sec, kernel-switch rate, and fairness index
Rollout plan with canary (5% traffic) + automated rollback if P95 regressions exceed threshold for any tenant tier
technical_notes: Fractional prefill split: enabling logical sub-phases inside a single request where the first micro-phase performs a kernel probe using a short prefix to estimate attention matrix sparsity and KV cache behavior

Kernel-probe signal: probe returns estimated decode throughput, per-head attention density, and memory footprint; runtime maps these to three kernel buckets: dense-optimized, sparse-optimized, and mixed/quantized path

Routing policy: micro-slices marked as latency-priority are steered to low-queue, latency-optimized execution lanes; batchy slices are aggregated on high-throughput lanes with larger microbatch windows

Tenant crediting: maintain per-tenant soft credits that replenish at a configurable rate; credits are consumed when scheduler assigns low-latency lane; deficit triggers proportional fairbackoff applied to throughput lanes
Speculative hedging: for ambiguous probes (confidence < threshold) schedule speculative hedges to both kernel types with cancellation on first completion to reduce misclassification tail
Overhead targets: kernel-probe must add <=0.6ms median to prefill for short prompts and <=1.5ms P95; split bookkeeping overhead must be <2% of scheduling CPU budget
experiments: Simulations: run tenant-mix traces (interactive-heavy, mixed, batch-heavy) on the discrete-event simulator to sweep split ratios [0.05..0.5] and probe confidence thresholds
Kernel probe ablation: compare accuracy and overhead of short-prefix probing lengths [8, 16, 32 tokens] and synthetic attention sparsity predictors (model signature vs runtime probe)
Hedging policy A/B: hedged vs non-hedged scheduling on ambiguous probes; evaluate cost increase vs P99 improvement
Credit policy tuning: linear vs exponential replenishment curves and max-credit caps to bound starvation and gaming

2026-03-11 Marco García: Uploaded simulator configs and baseline trace sample sets. Observed that naive splitting at 25% increases scheduler context switches by ~12% in CPU profile. Need to optimize slice metadata representation.

2026-03-12 Priya Nair (SRE): Flagged potential operational risk: per-tenant credit map will increase etcd write load if persisted. Recommend caching credits in-memory with periodic writeback and audit logs only on boundary events.

2026-03-12 Evan Liu (ML infra): Reviewed kernel-probe idea; suggested adding attention-head histogram export to better map to sparse kernels. Also proposed an ML classifier trained on historical runs to avoid probes for stable tenants.

2026-03-13 Marco García: Ran preliminary sim sweep (prefix=16 tokens) — latency tenants P95 improved by 12% with split=0.15 and probe confidence threshold 0.7. Throughput tenants dropped by 3.8%. Uploading results to simulator link. Next: integrate speculative hedging and optimize probe overhead.
